catalog_quote: 4.2. THE STRESS RULE. I start with a descriptive statement of the stress rule. (12) a. Final syllable is stressed if it contains a long vowel with a coda; b. else penult is stressed if it contains a long vowel; c. else antepenult is stressed. Using the investigated data, the success of the stress rule is 90.4%.10 ... 10. Nathan's (1973a) and Hughes' (2020:138) stress rule, “final if closed else penult,” has a 68% success rate on the same data with the same assumptions about intonation. ... An addendum to the clause (12b) of the stress rule is that closed penultimate syllables also attract stress. The only word-medial codas are first halves of geminate consonants. The effect of the geminate can only be seen where the vowel in the penult is short (16a). (2) Deciding source is a 2022 peer-reviewed phonology article in Oceanic Linguistics with rater-based stress location data (515 headwords, 81.9% inter-rater agreement) and duration measurements; it explicitly evaluates the competing Nathan 1973 / Hughes 2020 rule. Hughes 2020 (held, read at pp. 138-145) independently confirms weight-sensitive right-edge stress, differing only in denying the antepenult clause; our record already carries that as the secondary-stress rule. sources.quote: 'Although Nauruan stress has been described in fairly simple terms (Nathan, 1973), there is no general agreement about stress patterns in the literature.' Summarizes Nathan's rules: '1. Stress penultimate with final open syllables. 2. Stress final with most (but not all) final closed syllables. 3. Stress initial with reduplications (most of which are frozen).' and Kayser's rules: '1. Stress first syllable of dissyllabic words. 2. For words with more than two syllables, stress the penult if it is long, or the antepenult if the penult is short. 3. For derived words, always stress the suffix. ...
sources.note: Only other Glottolog 'phonology' reference; its stress section (pp. 61-62) relays Kayser 1936's 'penult if long, else antepenult' rule, an independent early witness for the weight-sensitive three-syllable window our record codes from Blumenfeld 2022.
